title: Ceva's Theorem in Higher Dimensions: The Cocycle Criterion for Simplex Concurrency
description: Answers the open question 'when do hypersurfaces bisect a simplex concurrently?' at the algebraic level underlying all Ceva/Menelaus formalizations. For an n-simplex whose concurrency point has positive barycentric weights w, the edge ratios r(i,j) = w_j/w_i satisfy a 1-cocycle law r(i,j)·r(j,k) = r(i,k); conversely any positive cocycle is reconstructed from a common point via w_i = r(b,i). The concurrency criterion: cevians of an n-simplex concur iff the classical Ceva product equals 1 on every triangular 2-face. The planar triangle Ceva product BD/DC·CE/EA·AF/FB = 1 is the single-triangle case.

overview.historicalContext:
Ceva's theorem (1678) for a triangle states that the cevians AD, BE, CF are concurrent iff (BD/DC)·(CE/EA)·(AF/FB) = 1. The parent file CevasTheoremOQ02.lean extends Ceva and Menelaus to spherical and hyperbolic triangles via a measure-function framework, and lists five open questions. The fourth asks: 'Extension to higher dimensions: when do hypersurfaces bisect a simplex concurrently?'

This entry answers that question at the algebraic level common to all of the gallery's Ceva work. The single planar Ceva equation is the n = 2 instance of a structural fact about n-simplices, and the goal here is to identify exactly which fact and prove both directions.
overview.problemStatement:
**Setup.** An n-simplex has vertices V₀,…,Vₙ (indexed by a type ι). A point P in its interior is given by positive barycentric weights w : ι → ℝ. For vertices i, j define the edge ratio r(i,j) = w_j / w_i. For the planar triangle these are exactly the cevian division ratios BD/DC, CE/EA, AF/FB.

**Theorem (forward).** If the edge ratios come from a common point, then they form a 1-cocycle: r(i,j)·r(j,k) = r(i,k), and the product of edge ratios around every closed walk of vertices equals 1 (the triangle case is the classical Ceva product).

**Theorem (converse / reconstruction).** If a positive edge-ratio assignment r is a cocycle, then it comes from a common point: there exist positive weights w with r(i,j) = w_j/w_i, given explicitly by w_i = r(b,i) for any base vertex b.

**Concurrency criterion.** For positive r the following are equivalent: (1) a concurrency point with those edge ratios exists; (2) r is a cocycle; (3) the classical Ceva product r(i,j)·r(j,k)·r(k,i) = 1 holds on every triangular 2-face.
overview.text: Higher-dimensional Ceva's theorem via the cocycle criterion for simplex concurrency. Edge ratios r(i,j) = w_j/w_i of a common point satisfy r(i,j)·r(j,k) = r(i,k); conversely any positive cocycle is reconstructed from a common point via w_i = r(b,i). Cevians of an n-simplex concur iff the planar Ceva product equals 1 on every triangular 2-face.
overview.proofStrategy:
The argument is the recognition that the planar Ceva product is a 1-coboundary on the simplex's 1-skeleton:

1. **Forward direction.** edge ratios of weights w are multiplicative by direct computation (field_simp); the triangle product collapses by chaining r(i,j)·r(j,k)·r(k,i) = r(i,k)·r(k,i) = r(i,i) = 1.
2. **Telescoping.** ∏_{t<m} f(t+1)/f(t) = f(m)/f(0) by induction; applied to f = w∘p along a closed walk p (p m = p 0) the product is w(p m)/w(p 0) = 1, giving Ceva for arbitrary cycles, not just triangles.
3. **Cube relation forces normalization.** From the triangle conditions alone, r(i,i)³ = 1 with r(i,i) > 0 forces r(i,i) = 1 (factor (x-1)(x²+x+1), second factor positive), then reciprocity r(i,j)·r(j,i) = 1, then multiplicativity by cancelling the nonzero factor r(k,i).
4. **Reconstruction.** Setting w_i = r(b,i), the cocycle law r(b,i)·r(i,j) = r(b,j) is exactly r(i,j) = w_j/w_i.
5. **Packaging.** Combining (1)–(4) yields the three-way concurrency equivalence.
keyInsights: The planar Ceva product BD/DC·CE/EA·AF/FB = 1 is the single-triangle instance of a 1-cocycle condition on a simplex's edge ratios — that is the structural reason it holds.
In dimension n the one triangle equation is replaced by the Ceva equation on EVERY triangular 2-face; those triangle conditions generate the whole concurrency relation.
Concurrency is exactly solvability: a positive edge-ratio assignment comes from a common point iff it is a coboundary r(i,j) = w_j/w_i, and the cocycle condition is precisely solvability.
The concurrency point is reconstructed explicitly — its barycentric coordinates are w_i = r(b,i) for any base vertex b — so the criterion is constructive, not just an existence statement.
The cube relation r(i,i)³ = 1 with positivity is what forces self-ratios to 1; this is the only nonlinear step and it is what makes the triangle conditions sufficient.
The closed-walk telescoping shows Ceva for arbitrary cycles (e.g. the 4-vertex loop of a tetrahedron), unifying all the ratio-product identities under one telescoping lemma.
prerequisites: Elementary group cohomology intuition (1-cocycles and coboundaries on a graph)

conclusion: The planar Ceva equation BD/DC·CE/EA·AF/FB = 1 is the n = 2 instance of a 1-cocycle condition on a simplex's edge ratios. In every dimension, cevians of an n-simplex concur precisely when the edge ratios form a cocycle, equivalently when the classical Ceva product equals 1 on every triangular 2-face; the concurrency point is reconstructed explicitly from any base vertex as w_i = r(b,i). This answers open question 4 of cevas-theorem-oq-02 at the algebraic level shared by all the gallery's Ceva/Menelaus entries, fully machine-checked with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
